crime_highlights: When Ms. Watson approached the bend she was travelling at approximately 118 kph.
The truck came to rest on its roof.
All four occupants suffered catastrophic injuries.
Mr. Tardif, Mr. Jackson and Mr. Murray were all pronounced dead at the scene.
Ms. Watson was extracted from the truck and transported to Invermere & District Hospital with life-threatening injuries.
rationale_highlights: Those factors may help the court assess the moral blameworthiness of the offender.
Substance use issues and fractured family structures are common intergenerational consequences of the residential school system.
Those substance use issues played a direct causative role in the offence that brings her before the court.
I find that Ms. Watson's moral blameworthiness is somewhat reduced in consideration of the Gladue factors present in her life, factors which played a key role in the offence she committed.
note: Para 140 also restates the reduction in blameworthiness.

crime_highlights: M.H. sexually touched [Victim 1] repeatedly from early 2016 until [Victim 1] moved out of the [Family] home in August 2021.
after he had been drinking, M.H. started coming into the bedroom [Victim 2] shared with her sisters
M.H. sexually touched [Victim 2] repeatedly from early 2016 until [Victim 2] moved out of the Family home in January 2022.
they left the [Family] home as soon as they were able, to avoid the sexual abuse that happened there
When I was in that hell of a home I wanted to die every day.

rationale_highlights: both Crown and defence submitted that Indigenous sentencing factors reduced M.H.'s moral blameworthiness from what the circumstances of the offence might otherwise dictate. I agree.
the reduced moral blameworthiness of an offender who was subjected to the classic negative intergenerational effects of colonialism
I accept that childhood trauma affected M.H.'s ability to assess right from wrong and might have led him to sexually interfere with [Victim 1] and [Victim 2].
it is reasonable to conclude that his Indigenous heritage may have played a role in bringing him before the court. This is a significant mitigating factor in sentencing.
note: Para 110 also states culpability is reduced.

crime_highlights: The victim awoke during the assault. R.T. told him to be quiet
The victim speaks to the significant ongoing pain and trauma he has experienced due to the assault.
The victim explains how he turned to substances to cope with the trauma and then, when the trauma became too much, attempted suicide on multiple occasions.
has caused him significant and ongoing trauma
rationale_highlights: The Indigenous sentencing report before me demonstrates that R.T. has been impacted by the effects of colonialism.
He experienced race-based bullying at school that conveyed the message that he did not belong.
I agree that these impacts must be considered even though R.T. has generally led a prosocial life.
colonialism and racism have had a significant impact on R.T.
Considering these factors, some restraint is in order.
